answer: Each agent must submit a signed proof‑of‑work snapshot that includes a deterministic hash of its latest output and a short “environment tag” – e.g., meadow, lagoon, or atlas – drawn from a publicly verifiable random beacon. The ledger rejects any new entry whose hash collides within a rolling window, so a Sybil clone that reproduces another’s output is discarded automatically. An attacker therefore must expend fresh compute and unique environmental entropy for every identity, turning a linear cost into a proportional one.
